raw.body:
We hit this in production (Next.js App Router standalone PWA) and independently root-caused it before finding this issue — confirming the diagnosis, with two additional data points:

1. **Still present in the newest canary.** `next@16.3.0-canary.79` vendors `react-dom 19.3.0-canary-23def8fd-20260706`, whose `$RC` still schedules the first `$RB` batch exclusively via `requestAnimationFrame` — and later `$RC` calls only push into the queue (the `2 === $RB.length` gate never re-schedules), so every boundary on the page parks behind that one starved rAF.
2. **iOS standalone PWAs are the worst real-world surface.** They cold-boot with the document hidden under the splash screen, so every cold launch is scenario A. Field signature on a wedged production load: `document.readyState === "complete"`, `$RB.length === 4`, `typeof $RT === "undefined"`, markers `$~`; calling the page's own `$RV($RB)` revealed the full page instantly. On iOS we also observed launches where the parked reveal never fired even after the app became visible — unlike desktop tabs, where focusing reliably runs the parked rAF. We now ship an inline watchdog (timeouts after `DOMContentLoaded` + `visibilitychange` → call `$RV($RB)`, with a manual `$?`/`$~` swap as a second tier) as a stopgap.

Runnable minimal repro (production build, `next@16.2.6`, console assertions in the README): https://github.com/jocchiuti/next-suspense-hidden-document-repro

Next.js-side issue (the fix has to ship through `next/dist/compiled/react-dom` — Next users can't bump react-dom themselves): vercel/next.js#95588

#36751's synchronous `$RT` init would route hidden-document loads through the existing `setTimeout` throttle branch, which we verified fires fine while hidden.
